latest_release.name: eCapture v2.12.0
latest_release.body:
## Breaking Changes / Migration

**Upgrade capture commands and receivers together.** eCapture now routes runtime logs and captured events through a repeatable `--output` flag. Files and outgoing TCP connections carry Protobuf v2 JSON Lines. WebSocket subscribers receive binary v2 records. The legacy flags below have been removed without aliases. [#1094](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/pull/1094)

| v2.11.0 configuration | v2.12.0 migration |
| --- | --- |
| `--eventaddr`, `--logaddr` / `-l` | Repeat `--output` once per destination. With no flag, logs and events go to `stdout`. Explicit destinations replace that default. Use `stdout` or `stderr` for labeled text, and a path, `file:///PATH`, or `tcp://HOST:PORT` for JSON Lines. |
| `--ecaptureq ws://HOST:PORT/PATH` | Use `--stream-listen ws://HOST:PORT/PATH`. Clients connect to eCapture and must negotiate the `ecapture.v2` subprotocol. Existing v1 clients need a v2 decoder. |
| Outgoing `ws://` or `wss://` event/log destinations | Migrate the receiver to JSON Lines over TCP, or have it subscribe to `--stream-listen`. |
| `--listen HOST:PORT` | Use `--config-listen HOST:PORT` for HTTP configuration updates. Both the HTTP and WebSocket listeners are disabled by default. |
| `--eventroratesize`, `--eventroratetime` | Remove these flags from startup scripts. File rotation has no CLI replacement. |
| `-m keylog` or `-m pcapng` with an implicit filename or redirected stdout | Specify a local `--keylogfile PATH` or `--pcapfile PATH` for the corresponding mode. Keep it separate from any `--output` file. |

For `tls` (OpenSSL/BoringSSL), `gotls`, and `gnutls`, the default `--model text --text-source pcapng` writes decoded messages and runtime logs to the selected outputs. In this mode, `--pcapfile` and `--keylogfile` can optionally save the packets and secrets used for decryption. In keylog and pcapng modes, an `--output` file receives only runtime logs.

```shell
# Keep decoded text on the terminal and also save structured records.
sudo ecapture tls --model text --text-source pcapng --output stdout --output capture.jsonl

# Save packets and TLS secrets for Wireshark, with runtime logs in a separate file.
sudo ecapture tls --model pcapng --pcapfile capture.pcapng --output runtime.jsonl
```

## What's Changed
* *: replace legacy output flags with Protobuf v2 streams by @cfc4n in https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/pull/1094
* *: publish collector runtime metadata to stream clients by @cfc4n in https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/pull/1095
* output: move subscription service to internal stream package by @cfc4n in https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/pull/1096
* cli: clarify capture options and command help by @cfc4n in https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/pull/1097


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/compare/v2.11.0...v2.12.0

detail.readme:
eCapture (旁观者)
Capture SSL/TLS plaintext with eBPF—no MITM proxy or custom CA installation.

English · 汉字

> [!IMPORTANT] > Supports Linux on x86_64 (kernel 4.18+), aarch64 (kernel **5.5+**), and LoongArch64 `loong64` (kernel **6.6+**). Android supports x86_64 and aarch64 with the existing kernel minimums. > Capturing data requires root privileges or specific [Linux capabilities](docs/minimum-privileges.md). > Does not support Windows or macOS. ---- - [Introduction](#introduction) - [Getting started](#getting-started) - [Download](#download) - [ELF binary file](#elf-binary-file) - [Docker image](#docker-image) - [Capture OpenSSL plaintext data](#capture-openssl-plaintext-data) - [Modules](#modules) - [OpenSSL module](#openssl-module) - [GoTLS module](#gotls-module) - [Other modules](#other-modules) - [Videos](#videos) - [Star History](#star-history) - [Security & operations](#security--operations) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [Compilation](#compilation) # Introduction * Captures TLS plaintext from applications using OpenSSL, BoringSSL, or GnuTLS, and data read or written through NSPR. * Supports plaintext capture for Go TLS programs, including HTTPS/TLS traffic in Go applications. * Captures commands entered in interactive Bash and Zsh sessions. * Audits MySQL queries and supports MySQL 5.6/5.7/8.0 and MariaDB. Run `ecapture --help` to list commands and global options. Use `ecapture tls --help` or `ecapture help tls` for TLS options and examples. You can view help as a regular user. # Getting started ## Download ### ELF binary file > [!TIP] > Supports Linux on x86_64, aarch64, and LoongArch64; Android supports x86_64 and aarch64. Download the ELF binary package from the [releases page](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/releases), extract it, and run: ```shell ecapture --help ``` ### Docker image > [!TIP] > Linux only. ```shell # Pull the Docker image docker pull gojue/ecapture:latest # Run it docker run --rm --privileged=true --net=host -v ${HOST_PATH}:${CONTAINER_PATH} gojue/ecapture ARGS ``` > **⚠️ Security note**: `--privileged=true` grants full host access. For production use, prefer specific capabilities instead. See the [Minimum Privileges Guide](docs/minimum-privileges.md#method-3-docker-with-specific-capabilities). See [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/gojue/ecapture) for more information. ## Capture OpenSSL plaintext data ```shell sudo ecapture tls ``` eCapture automatically detects the system's OpenSSL library and selects a capture interface: it prefers an up Ethernet interface on the lowest-metric IPv4/IPv6 default route, then falls back to interface traffic counters or an up interface. A startup warning names the selected interface and explains how to override it with `-i eth0` or `--ifname eth0`. Only that interface is captured; use `-i lo` for loopback traffic. Generate an HTTPS request with an OpenSSL-linked client to see the reconstructed request and response. This synthetic HTTP/1.1 example illustrates the text format: ```text [2026-01-01T12:00:00.000000000Z] http/1.1 request 192.0.2.1:43210 -> 192.0.2.2:443 host="example.com" domain_source="Host" connection="17-4-client/192.0.2.1:43210--192.0.2.2:443/tcp#2" GET / HTTP/1.1 Host: example.com ``` > 📄 For output formats and verification examples, see [docs/example-outputs.md](docs/example-outputs.md). ## Modules Linux builds include all eight modules below. Android builds include `tls`, `gotls`, and `bash`. * bash: captures bash commands * zsh: captures zsh commands * gnutls: captures plaintext from GnuTLS libraries without needing a CA certificate * gotls: captures plaintext communication from Go programs using TLS/HTTPS * mysqld: captures SQL queries from MySQL 5.6/5.7/8.0 and MariaDB * nspr (alias `nss`): captures data read and written through NSPR * postgres: captures SQL sent through the simple query protocol on PostgreSQL 10 and later * tls: captures TLS plaintext from applications using OpenSSL or BoringSSL You can use `ecapture -h` to view the full list of subcommands. ### OpenSSL module eCapture searches standard library paths for `libssl`. Use `--libssl` to select a specific library. If the target program is statically linked, you can set the program path directly as the value of the `--libssl` flag. The OpenSSL module supports three output modes: - `pcap`/`pcapng` mode stores encrypted network packets and TLS secrets in `pcap-NG` format. - `keylog`/`key` mode saves TLS handshake keys to a file. - `text` mode defaults to `--text-source=pcapng`, reconstructing complete HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 messages from live pcapng and DSB data. The capture interface is selected automatically; use `-i eth0` to override it. Use `--text-source=hook` to capture plaintext through function hooks instead (no interface required). For OpenSSL, GoTLS, and GnuTLS, repeat `--output` to choose multiple destinations. The default is `stdout`; explicit destinations replace that default. `stdout` and `stderr` render readable records with `log_type`/`module` labels. In `-m pcapng` mode, the terminal shows only operational logs. Files and `tcp://host:port` use Protobuf v2 JSON Lines. In text mode they carry both operational logs and captured events; in keylog/pcapng mode an output **file contains only operational logs**, while TCP carries both record types. Use `--keylogfile`/`--pcapfile` for native artifacts, with explicit filenames required in the corresponding mode and no default native files. `--stream-listen ws://127.0.0.1:28257/` starts a separate Protobuf v2 subscription listener requiring the `ecapture.v2` subprotocol. `--config-listen 127.0.0.1:28256` starts the HTTP configuration service. Both listeners are disabled by default. The old `--listen`, `--eventaddr`, `--logaddr`, `--ecaptureq` and event rotation flags are removed without compatibility aliases. See the [output API](docs/event-forward-api.md) for the complete mode matrix and receiver migration. #### Live decryption for text output `tls`, `gotls`, and `gnutls` default to the `pcapng` text source and automatically select a capture interface when `-i` is omitted. All three accept `--text-source hook` for function-hook capture. GoTLS still requires `--elfpath` to identify the target binary. Use `-m text --text-source=pcapng` with `tls`, `gotls`, or `gnutls` to reconstruct complete HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 messages from the captured network stream. Each message includes direction, timestamp, IP/port tuple, connection identity, and an HTTP/2 stream ID when applicable. `host` comes from the HTTP `Host` header or HTTP/2 `:authority`; `domain_source="server_ip"` marks a fallback to the server IP. Output goes to `--output` (stdout by default). Raw pcapng and a standalone keylog are disabled by default; specify `--pcapfile` or `--keylogfile` to save either artifact. ```shell sudo ecapture tls -m text --text-source=pcapng -i eth0 --output stdout --output /tmp/http.jsonl 'tcp port 443' sudo ecapture gotls -m text --text-source=pcapng --elfpath /path/to/go-client -i eth0 --pcapfile /tmp/raw.pcapng 'tcp port 443' sudo ecapture gnutls -m text --text-source=pcapng --gnutls /path/to/libgnutls.so -i eth0 'tcp port 443' ``` The decryptor waits for TLS secrets that may appear in a DSB after the corresponding packets. HTTP/3 over QUIC v1/v2 has GoTLS test fixtures; support depends on the TLS backend supplying the required secrets. The following options require text mode with the pcapng source: | Option | Output / selection | | --- | --- | | `--text-raw` | Authenticated TLS/QUIC STREAM bytes and QUIC DATAGRAM messages | | `--text-http-events` | Incremental HTTP/1.x, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, SSE and HTTP/2 gRPC events | | `--text-max-decoded-body N` | Per-message gzip expansion limit in bytes; requires HTTP events; zero keeps content encoding | | `--text-protocol dot\|doh\|doq\|mqtt\|redis` | Explicit application parser; MQTT 3.1.1 and fixed-length RESP2/RESP3 | | `--text-tls-upgrade smtp\|imap\|pop3\|ldap\|postgres\|mysql\|connect\|https-connect` | One explicit STARTTLS/SSLRequest/CONNECT negotiation; HTTPS CONNECT includes one inner TLS layer | | `--text-udp-protocol dtls` | DTLS 1.2 ECDHE-RSA AES-128/256-GCM records; the default UDP protocol is QUIC | Structured events use lossless hex plus `metadata` JSON, preserving headers, trailers, message/stream IDs, early-data status and TLS depth, including events with no payload. Stream chunks carry offsets/end markers; datagrams retain message boundaries without invented stream offsets. Application selection is explicit, not automatic ALPN routing. Raw, HTTP-event and explicit application modes are mutually exclusive. HTTP reload uses the corresponding underscore JSON keys; omitted module options reset to their zero defaults. Mail/database upgrades negotiate TLS; use `--text-raw` for application bytes without a supported parser. gRPC events preserve schema-free Protobuf bytes. Operational logs contain payload-free diagnostics. ECH still requires `ECH_SECRET`/`ECH_CONFIG` material that current probes do not capture; upgrading the decryptor alone does not enable live ECH. DTLS/DATAGRAM do not imply WebRTC, WebTransport or MASQUE decoding. With v1.4.0, some zero-length-client-CID QUIC loopback captures still fail connection routing; the maintained DoQ/DATAGRAM baseline uses 8-byte client CIDs. To verify the source independently, add `--pcapfile /tmp/raw.pcapng` to the capture command and send a request with a unique path or response token. After stopping eCapture, preload only its embedded secrets with Wireshark >= 4.4 to handle DSBs arriving after their packets, then compare TLS stream 0: ```shell keys=$(mktemp) editcap --extract-secrets /tmp/raw.pcapng - >"$keys" tshark -n -r /tmp/raw.pcapng -o "tls.keylog_file:$keys" -q -z follow,tls,ascii,0 rm -f -- "$keys" ``` The optional file receives the same pcapng bytes as the live SDK stream. Terminal records and JSON files distinguish operational logs from captured events. JSON and Protobuf share the v2 schema; receivers must preserve TEXT metadata and save native KEYLOG/PCAPNG bytes by format. Subscriptions receive future events; a late pcapng connection starts an independent fragment without historical packets or keys. See the [v2 protocol](protobuf/PROTOCOLS.md) and [receiver example](examples/ecaptureq_client/README.md). #### Pcap mode Supports TLS-encrypted HTTP `1.0/1.1/2.0` over TCP and HTTP/3 (QUIC) over UDP. Use `-m pcapng` (alias `-m pcap`) with `--pcapfile` to name the required local capture file. Use `-i` to override the automatically selected interface. ```shell sudo ecapture tls -m pcap -i eth0 --pcapfile=ecapture.pcapng tcp port 443 ``` This command saves captured network packets and TLS secrets in a pcapng file. Wireshark uses its embedded secrets to decrypt supported TLS traffic. > 📄 For pcapng verification, see [docs/example-outputs.md](docs/example-outputs.md#tls-module--pcapng-mode). #### Keylog mode You can specify `-m keylog` or `-m key` together with the `--keylogfile` option. `--keylogfile` must name an explicit local artifact file; there is no default filename. The captured OpenSSL TLS master secret is saved to `--keylogfile`. You can also enable `tcpdump` capture and then open the file in Wireshark, setting the master secret path to view plaintext packets. ```shell sudo ecapture tls -m keylog --keylogfile=openssl_keylog.log ``` You can also use `tshark` for real-time decryption and display: ```shell tshark -o tls.keylog_file:openssl_keylog.log -Y http -T fields -e http.file_data -f "port 443" -i eth0 ``` #### Text mode ```shell sudo ecapture tls -m text ``` This reconstructs HTTP messages using the default `pcapng` text source. To capture plaintext bytes from TLS function hooks, use `sudo ecapture tls -m text --text-source hook` (no interface required). ### GoTLS module Similar to the OpenSSL module. #### `gotls` command Capture TLS plaintext data. Step 1: ```shell sudo ecapture gotls --elfpath=/path/to/go-client ``` Step 2: ```shell /path/to/go-client ``` #### More help ```shell ecapture gotls -h ``` ### Other modules Modules such as `bash`, `mysqld`, and `postgres` can also be used. You can view the full list with `ecapture -h`. ## Videos * YouTube video: [How to use eCapture v0.1.0](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CoDIjEQCvvA "eCapture User Manual") * [eCapture: supports capturing plaintext of Go TLS/HTTPS traffic](https://medium.com/@cfc4ncs/ecapture-supports-capturing-plaintext-of-golang-tls-https-traffic-f16874048269) ## eCaptureQ GUI application [eCaptureQ](https://github.com/gojue/ecaptureq) is a cross-platform graphical client for eCapture that visualizes eBPF-based TLS capture capabilities. It provides an interface for analyzing encrypted traffic without needing a CA certificate. It supports two modes: * Integrated mode: unified Linux/Android execution * Remote mode: Windows/macOS/Linux clients connect to a remote eCapture service This eCapture version requires a client with Protobuf v2 support and the `ecapture.v2` WebSocket subprotocol. Check the selected client release against the [receiver contract](docs/event-forward-api.md#receiving-v2); older v1 clients cannot connect without an update. ### Event forwarding [Event forwarding projects](./docs/event-forward.md) ### Video demonstration https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8b7a84d-58eb-4fdb-9843-f775c97bdbfb 🔗 [GitHub repository](https://github.com/gojue/ecaptureq) ### Protobuf protocols For details of the Protobuf log schema used by eCapture/eCaptureQ, see: - [protobuf/PROTOCOLS.md](./protobuf/PROTOCOLS.md) ## Star History # Security & operations - [**Security policy**](SECURITY.md) — vulnerability reporting and supported versions - [**Minimum privileges**](docs/minimum-privileges.md) — required Linux capabilities and least-privilege configuration - [**Defense & detection**](docs/defense-detection.md) — how to detect and defend against unauthorized usage - [**Performance benchmarks**](docs/performance-benchmarks.md) — repeatable overhead and event-loss measurements - [**Release verification**](docs/release-verification.md) — how to verify the integrity of release artifacts # Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for details on submitting patches and the contribution workflow. # Compilation ## Custom compilation You can customize the features you want, such as setting the `uprobe` offset address to support statically linked OpenSSL libraries. Refer to the [compilation guide](./docs/compilation.md) for detailed instructions. Loong64 releases are cross-built on Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 with LLVM 22.1.8. Use `TARGET_ARCH=loong64`; the sysroot, BTF, verification steps, and current runtime validation limits are documented in [Loong64 build and validation](./docs/loong64-support.md). ## Remote configuration updates After eCapture is running, you can dynamically modify configurations through HTTP interfaces. Refer to the [HTTP API documentation](./docs/remote-config-update-api.md). ## Event forwarding eCapture supports multiple event-forwarding methods. You can forward events to packet capture software such as Burp Suite. For details, refer to the [Event Forwarding API documentation](./docs/event-forward-api.md).
